messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PDINC-2026-448 — billing.ingest.consumer-lag (P1) :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Triggered at 2026-03-14T15:20:10Z. Symptoms: Kafka consumer lag > 1h on billing-ingest-prod, token-count propagation stalled. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PDINC-2026-448

marta: Ack'd. I'm on call. Starting triage — will check consumer group offsets and ingestion lags. @liam can you join?

liam: on it. preliminary: offsets show partition spikes. Running quick check:
```
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --group billing-ingest-consumer --describe
# PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
# 23         1245000         1249500         4500
# 24         1244800         1249500         4700
```
Looks like consumer lag ~4.5k-5k messages concentrated on a small subset of partitions.

nick: Billing FYI — if token counts don't reconcile we may need to pause invoice finalization. How long has this been going on?

marta: From alert window metrics, the lag started ~15:05Z and climbed steadily. Estimated 75 minutes. Could affect token counts up to ~1 hour behind realtime. Assessing customer impact now.

eve: Customer-success: flagging high-priority customers with billing deadlines today. I'll prepare a temporary communication list if we need invoice holds.

sam: Quick note — we saw a recent deploy to ingest workers at 14:50Z that changed consumer parallelism from 4 -> 3. Rolling that back might help. Any correlation logs? 

liam: Checking deployment logs... yes, deploy id deploy-2026-03-14-1450 adjusted worker-count. CPU on remaining workers is spiking. Command to scale up back:
```
kubectl scale deployment billing-ingest-workers --replicas=5 -n prod
```

marta: Doing scale now.

incident-bot: automation: increased replicas to 5 (deploy billing-ingest-workers). Rolling restart started.

liam: Consumers catching up slowly. Lags dropping: partition 23 lag -> 1200, 24 -> 1500.

marta: Good. Hold for 5m and re-evaluate. @nick please prepare invoice hold playbook if counts still off after catchup.

nick: Roger. Preparing hold flags and a list of invoices generated in the last 2 hours to freeze if needed. Also opening a temporary invoice-hold ticket.

pagerduty-bot: Alert transitioned to 'acknowledged' by marta at 2026-03-14T15:27:05Z.

liam: Follow-up: seeing occasional consumer rebalances. Examining broker-side replication health. No under-replicated partitions. Suspect resource contention during deploy.

marta: Monitoring token count delta metric now. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/billing/token-delta?from=now-6h&to=now

sam: Also kicking off a one-off reconcile run to patch downstream counts for the window. Command:
```
/scripts/reconcile_tokens --from "2026-03-14T14:30:00Z" --to "2026-03-14T16:00:00Z" --dry-run
```

marta: Start real run after dry-run passes. Execute with rate-limit to avoid overwhelming DB.

sam: Dry-run done — no catastrophic diffs. Starting real run with concurrency 2.

incident-bot: Job reconcile_tokens-3176543210 started by sam. ETA ~18 minutes.

eve: Notifying 4 customers with imminent invoices about a possible delay. Template posted to #customer-comms-drafts.

nick: Reconcile job showing progress, reconciling ~8k tokens per minute. Projected finish ~14 minutes. If successful, we can avoid invoice hold.

liam: Consumer lag now <200 across partitions. Good sign.

marta: Thanks. Keep monitoring. If reconcile completes and token deltas are within tolerance (<0.1%), we'll clear incident.

incident-bot: reconcile_tokens-3176543210 completed successfully. Changes applied: 2,345 token deltas corrected. No customer-facing invoice adjustments required at this time.

sam: verifying downstream ledgers match; spot-checks look good.

nick: Cancelling temporary invoice-hold ticket. Will keep an eye for any anomalies during invoice run.

eve: Updating customers to say issue mitigated and we're monitoring. :white_check_mark:

marta: Handing off to nick for follow-up post-incident analysis and postmortem. Next oncall @nick takes over at 16:00Z. Action items: 1) postmortem runbook 2) add guardrail to prevent consumer-count regression on deploy 3) add automated pre-deploy check for consumer parallelism.

nick: Acked. I'll own the postmortem and run the deploy guardrail RFC.

marta: Incident resolved — closing PDINC-2026-448. Good job team. :tada:
